summary.text: Greta Neubauer is a Democratic member of the Wisconsin State Assembly from District 66 who is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Republican Gina Cefalu Paulick.
She has been the Assembly's Democratic minority leader since January 2022, according to Ballotpedia.

paragraphs.text: Greta Neubauer was born and raised in Racine, Wisconsin, graduated from the Prairie School in 2010 and earned a B.A. in history from Middlebury College in 2015.

Her career experience includes working as a legislative aide to State Representative Cory Mason and serving as director and co-founder of the Fossil Fuel Divestment Student Network and co-founder of Divest Middlebury.
She has been board chair of the Racine Hospitality Center and has volunteered with groups including the Racine Interfaith Coalition and the NAACP-Racine Branch.

Neubauer first won the District 66 seat in a special election held January 16, 2018, after Cory Mason resigned from the Assembly following his election as mayor of Racine, and she assumed office on January 27, 2018.
She has been re-elected in each general election since, most recently in 2024.

Ballotpedia lists her 2025-2026 committee assignments as Assembly Organization, Employment Relations, Rules, Legislative Organization, Joint Legislative Council and the Joint Survey Committee on Retirement Systems.
